LESSON 33 / ADDITIONAL INTERVIEW CONCEPT
Successful controls, disabled, readonly and
hidden

Form submission includes successful named controls. Disabled controls are omitted. Read-only text
controls remain submitted, and hidden inputs are submitted but can be modified by the client.

A checkout form submits a user ID and an order reference.
Form · name="user" readonly · Kamal · Submitted data · name="coupon" disabled · user=Kamal · SAVE10 · orderId=42 · coupon omitted · hidden: orderId=42

Read the diagram: Read-only user and hidden orderId are submitted; disabled coupon is not. The
server must verify all values, including hidden ones.

<form>
  <input name="user" value="Kamal" readonly>
  <input name="coupon" value="SAVE10" disabled>
  <input type="hidden" name="orderId" value="42">
  <button>Submit</button>
</form>
Expected result: Form data includes user and orderId, not coupon.
Interview question: Can hidden inputs be trusted for authorization?
Answer: No. Clients can modify them; check permissions on the server.
Practice: Inspect the submitted request in DevTools.
